failure_summary.description: Follow-up preferences triggered fresh searches instead of retrieving compatible cached results and filtering only the changed criteria.
Results were not saved, were saved through duplicate inline calls, or were saved using variables that had never been assigned.
Some calls used incorrect argument shapes or fields, malformed preference values, or an overly narrow rating bound.

patch.reasoning: The cache-reuse and result-saving failures already directly contradict explicit rules in the skill, so repeating those rules would not patch a gap. This edit addresses uncovered parameter-shape and rating-threshold cases from the batch.

edits.target: - Pass only criteria supported by the conversation, map each value to the field that expresses it, and preserve the user's entity text. For example, put a state abbreviation in `state`, not `city`. Use the tool's accepted format for preferences such as time ranges; use an example format only when supported by the tool. Distinguish hotel stars (`stars`) from guest ratings (`rating`); for a supported “at least N stars” constraint, use the inclusive range from N to the field's maximum, and for an exact category use the same value as both bounds. Do not add unrelated preferences.
edits.content: - Pass only criteria supported by the conversation, map each value to the field that expresses it, and preserve the user's entity text. For example, put a state abbreviation in `state`, not `city`. Check argument types against the tool schema: a single airport name or code is a scalar string (for example, `end_airport="ANC"`), not a one-item list. Use the tool's accepted format for preferences such as time ranges; use an example format only when supported by the tool. Distinguish hotel stars (`stars`) from guest ratings (`rating`): for a supported “at least N stars” constraint, use the inclusive range from N to the field's maximum; for a guest-rating floor, use `[N, 5]`; use equal bounds only for an explicitly exact rating or category. Do not add unrelated preferences.
